physical_mismatches.reason: 3D thermal stack (silicon IC, solder TIM, copper heat spreader, thermal grease, heatsink) models realistic cooling path; however, solder balls and motherboard excluded from model (noted in Fig. 4 caption). HotSniper (prior work) modeled only 45nm Gainestown with Hotspot-6.0; this work uses 3D-ICE for transient modeling of modern nodes.

Floorplan scaled uniformly across technology nodes (50% area reduction per node) with fixed core aspect ratio (3×2), but global wire delays do not scale proportionally. Paper acknowledges in Section III-E that die size historically remains constant as logic density increases, affecting critical timing path lengths.

Non-uniform temperature initialization implemented to model background OS tasks and recently context-switched workloads; however, exact thermal state of real hardware prior to ROI execution unknown and simulated only qualitatively.

Power model (McPAT v1.2) tuned using Cdyn validation against Intel Core i5 10310U (14nm mobile) and Core i7-1165G7 (10nm SuperFin) via Intel TAT. Validation error 11% (14nm) and 20% (10nm). 7nm model extrapolated; no real silicon validation available for 7nm case study.

Single-threaded SPEC2006 execution on single core; symmetric multi-threading (SMT) capability modeled (2 threads/core) but not exercised in primary results. Multi-threaded workload behavior and contention effects not characterized.

studio_assumptions: -Area scaling 50% per technology node (14nm→10nm→7nm) with constant floorplan layout and core placement
-Dynamic power (Cdyn) decreases 20% per technology node following transistor scaling trends
-Leakage power and area scaled to match advanced nodes using standard transistor scaling assumptions
-Frequency fixed at 5 GHz (turbo boost V-f point) and voltage at 1.4 V across all process nodes
-Heatsink model HS483-ND with fan at 6000 rpm remains identical across technology nodes; die area reduction increases thermal resistance Ψ per node
-Hotspot definition parameterized: Tth=80°C (max junction minus margin), MLTDth=25°C (timing slack), radius=1mm (global wire delay in clock cycle)
-Hotspot severity metric composed of three parameterized sigmoid functions calibrated from industry data: σdf (device failure at 115°C), σM and σT (timing margins with non-linear temperature effects)
-Background thermal state initialized with idle OS workload trace prior to ROI to model realistic multi-tasking environment
-Cache warm-up performed before 200M instruction ROI simulation; transient thermal dynamics captured with 1M cycle time steps
-Floorplan inspired by Intel Skylake; 50 functional units modeled compared to 6 units in prior HotSniper work
